scope_note: Ten candidates span ambulatory practice-management applications, configurable EMR/HMIS platforms, integrated clinic/small-facility suites, an LIS subsystem, and a developer platform. Scores are provisional screening judgments, not directly interchangeable rankings, adoption approvals, security audits, clinical-safety reviews, compliance certifications, or production-readiness assessments.

scoring_rubric.interpretation: Use the aggregate score only as a preliminary evidence screen. A high score does not establish turnkey clinic coverage, local payer fit, interoperability conformance, Arabic/RTL acceptance, legal eligibility, clinical safety, privacy compliance, security, or production readiness. Missing evidence remains unknown and lowers confidence; scores do not replace eligibility gates.

records.name: OpenEMR
records.category: Ambulatory EHR and medical practice-management system
records.clinic_fit: Highest direct clinic/practice-management fit in this set: documented registration, scheduling, encounters/charting, prescriptions, billing/claims, labs, referrals, patient portal, multiple facilities, and REST/FHIR/SMART APIs.
records.license: GPL-3.0 in canonical root LICENSE; Composer metadata says GPL-3.0-or-later (clarify discrepancy). OSI-approved.
records.license_notes: Review the GPL metadata discrepancy and inventory all third-party dependencies/notices and separately offered support/hosting services before redistribution.
records.maintenance_security: Current activity and release 8.4.1 (2026-09-20) were observed. Release 8.4.0 disclosed multiple critical/high/medium security fixes across RCE, SQL injection, SSRF, authorization/IDOR, PHI and portal/FHIR paths. The review is not a complete security audit; patch status and deployment hardening are material gates.
records.interoperability: Official docs describe Standard REST, FHIR R4, US Core, SMART on FHIR, OAuth/OIDC, bulk export and CCD. Confirm exact installed version, enabled resources and local profiles.
records.arabic_rtl: Official feature page lists Arabic, UTF-8 and RTL; translation completeness, terminology quality and end-to-end bidirectional QA remain unverified.
records.confidence: Medium-high for identity, clinic fit, current activity, stated APIs, license identity and stated Arabic/RTL support; medium for security posture, deployment suitability and implementation depth.

records.name: GNU Health HMIS
records.clinic_fit: Broad primary-care and facility scope: patient records, encounters, appointments, prescriptions, billing, pharmacy/stock, laboratory, imaging and administration, using selectable modules and federation.
records.license: GPL-3.0-or-later for HMIS source; documentation and bundled components have separate notices/licenses. OSI-approved GPLv3 family.
records.license_notes: Review Tryton and documentation/component licenses in the exact bundle; GPL-3+ has copyleft obligations for covered redistributed works.
records.maintenance_security: Canonical repository is non-archived with active 5.0.x releases and activity at the checked date. Official security guidance and advisory process exist, but no full audit, dependency SBOM, penetration report or response SLA was established.
records.interoperability: GNU Health Federation and a FHIR/REST server are documented, but official docs explicitly describe FHIR as in development, read/search-oriented, incomplete and without write functionality.
records.arabic_rtl: Gettext/Weblate localization is documented; Arabic translation completeness and RTL behavior are unknown.
records.confidence: Medium-high for documented scope, licensing and maintenance; medium for security/operations; low for Arabic/RTL, regulatory status, clinical validation and production readiness.

records.name: OpenMRS
records.clinic_fit: Configurable patient-centered record and extensible clinical-program foundation with registration, charting, appointments and queues; clinics must assemble the final distribution, UI apps, modules and integrations.
records.license: MPL-2.0 with OpenMRS Healthcare Disclaimer for core; OSI-approved MPL-2.0. Modules/distributions require separate review.
records.license_notes: Core license does not automatically cover all modules, distributions, terminologies or transitive dependencies. Preserve required notices and review the healthcare disclaimer.
records.maintenance_security: Active commit history and release 2.8.10 (2026-10-06) were observed. Private vulnerability reporting is documented; no complete dependency, penetration or module-supply-chain audit was performed.
records.interoperability: Official materials identify REST and FHIR, including an initially R4-oriented FHIR2 module and integration targets; test exact resources and conformance against target systems.
records.arabic_rtl: Official product material names Arabic translation and RTL capability; quality and completeness in the selected distribution/modules require acceptance testing.
records.confidence: Medium-high for core scope, architecture, APIs, licensing and stated i18n/RTL capability; lower for workflow completeness, module security and Arabic/RTL quality.

records.name: Bahmni
records.category: Integrated EMR/HIS distribution for clinics and hospitals
records.clinic_fit: Integrated community distribution combining OpenMRS, OpenELIS, Odoo, PACS and Bahmni components for registration, point of care, encounters, appointments, treatments, investigations, billing and inventory; suitable where a composed stack is preferred.
records.license: Multi-license: bahmni-package is AGPL-3.0-or-later; core/frontend include MPL-2.0 texts; upstream components have separate terms and an AGPL-to-MPL-with-healthcare-disclaimer transition is described by the project.
records.license_notes: Review every repository, release, dependency and upstream component. A healthcare-disclaimer variant is not assumed to be OSI-approved solely because standard MPL-2.0 is approved.
records.maintenance_security: Recent commits were observed across package/core/frontend repositories, but the package release stream was unclear. Private vulnerability reporting exists; no full stack/dependency audit, hardening baseline or SLA was established.
records.interoperability: REST/FHIR APIs, Atom Feed synchronization and integrations with OpenMRS/OpenELIS/Odoo/PACS are documented; distribution-wide conformance and bidirectional workflows are unverified.
records.arabic_rtl: i18n infrastructure exists; reviewed community evidence says it was not Arabic/RTL-ready and references an RTL work item. Current complete Arabic/RTL support is not established.
records.confidence: Medium for product scope, architecture, licensing, deployment and APIs; reduced by distributed product surface, mixed licensing and incomplete evidence on security, Arabic/RTL and multi-clinic governance.

records.name: OpenClinic GA
records.category: Integrated hospital and clinic information-management system
records.clinic_fit: Broad resource-constrained clinic/facility system: patient records, encounters, ADT, scheduling, pharmacy, billing/insurance, laboratory, imaging and reporting; interoperability claims include HL7/FHIR and DICOM/PACS.
records.license: LGPL-2.0 per canonical SourceForge project page; an IDB profile labels the project GPLv2, so clarify before redistribution. OSI-listed historical LGPLv2.0.
records.license_notes: Treat LGPLv2 as stronger project-specific evidence but verify exact current bundle and every third-party component; the conflicting IDB label is material.
records.maintenance_security: SourceForge release/source artifacts were modified 2026-10-10, but public governance, issue/PR history, current security policy, SBOM and release notes were not established. Older technical/security documentation creates a material assurance gap.
records.interoperability: Project material claims HL7/FHIR, DICOM/PACS and analyzer interfaces; conformance profiles, authentication, version compatibility and integration tests were not documented in reviewed sources.
records.arabic_rtl: English, French, Dutch, Spanish and Portuguese are named; Arabic and RTL are unverified.
records.confidence: Moderate on stated scope, release artifacts, API claims and project-page license; lower for current security, test maturity, dependency licensing, Arabic/RTL and deployment reproducibility.

records.name: Open Hospital
records.category: Lightweight HIMS for health centers and hospitals
records.clinic_fit: Strong small-clinic/health-center candidate for constrained connectivity: registration, visits/encounters, appointments, therapy/prescriptions, pharmacy/stock, billing, labs, vaccination and basic inpatient workflows. Mature path is desktop/portable or LAN client/server; REST/API and React UI are WIP.
records.license: GPL-3.0 for application code; documentation policies separately state CC BY-SA 4.0. OSI-approved GPLv3.
records.license_notes: Review Maven/npm third-party dependencies and notices separately; GPLv3 copyleft obligations apply to covered redistributed works.
records.maintenance_security: Release v1.15.2 on 2026-10-12 and recent commits. No host SECURITY.md was found; reviewed API security config disables CSRF and permits broad methods/headers subject to configured origins. This is a hardening concern, not a complete security assessment.
records.interoperability: REST/OpenAPI evidence exists, but no primary evidence of HL7/FHIR conformance or stable external interoperability contract was reviewed.
records.arabic_rtl: Arabic resource exists but includes untranslated strings; supported RTL layout/QA is unknown.
records.confidence: Medium-high for documented features, architecture, license, release activity and deployment; medium for security posture, API maturity, Arabic/RTL, multi-clinic capability and clinical/regulatory suitability.

records.name: Marley Health
records.category: Open-source healthcare HIS application for Frappe/ERPNext
records.clinic_fit: Strong provisional clinic fit for appointments, encounters, prescriptions, labs, procedures, rehabilitation, referrals, insurance, portal and service-unit modeling, provided the clinic accepts the Frappe/ERPNext Bench dependency.
records.license: GPL-3.0 for Marley app; patient portal package declares MIT; Frappe/ERPNext and transitive components need separate review.
records.license_notes: Inventory the platform, portal, dependencies and any hosted/support service terms separately; GPL copyleft obligations apply to covered redistributed works.
records.maintenance_security: Recent v16.6.0 release and commits through 2026-10-07; CI, CodeQL and permission tests are present. No SECURITY.md was found; Dependabot covers GitHub Actions, not the full Python/Node/Bench graph. No full security or dependency audit.
records.interoperability: FHIR-oriented design and REST/whitelisted Frappe methods are documented; no public conformance schema, external lab adapter, SMART profile or certification was verified.
records.arabic_rtl: Portal tests include Arabic strings, Arabic locale/date handling and direction logic; full desk, report, print and upstream ERPNext Arabic/RTL coverage is unknown.
records.confidence: Medium-high for repository, license, feature model and maintenance facts; medium for clinic fit and deployment/operations maturity.

records.name: CARE HMIS
records.category: FHIR-inspired open-source HMIS and clinical-operations platform
records.clinic_fit: Broad clinic/hospital operations beyond booking: registration, appointments/queues, encounters, prescriptions/dispensing, diagnostics, referrals, billing, inventory and facility operations. Requires the separately maintained frontend and configuration.
records.license: MIT for CARE backend and frontend repositories. OSI-approved MIT; dependencies, plugins, terminology and services retain separate terms.
records.license_notes: Review both repositories, dependencies, plugins, integrations and any hosted/implementation service terms; MIT does not confer clinical or regulatory approval.
records.maintenance_security: Active backend/frontend repository activity observed. Security policy covers latest version only and supplies a reporting channel; no full audit, supported-version matrix or certification was established. Compose uses a mutable object-storage image tag, creating reproducibility/supply-chain risk.
records.interoperability: Official product materials claim FHIR R5-aligned APIs and terminology support; specific conformance profiles/version guarantees and production interoperability tests were not established.
records.arabic_rtl: Checked frontend locale set did not include Arabic and no RTL mode was evidenced; i18n infrastructure exists but readiness is unknown.
records.confidence: Medium-high for scope, architecture, license and maintenance signals; medium for deployment/security readiness; low for Arabic/RTL and clinical/regulatory status.

records.name: OpenELIS Global
records.category: Open-source laboratory information system / clinic-adjacent diagnostics subsystem
records.clinic_fit: Deliberately limited clinic fit: a strong lab subsystem for orders, patient/sample identity, specimen workflows, analyzers, results, surveillance and interoperability; not a general practice-management EHR.
records.license: MPL-2.0 in the canonical repository. OSI-approved; submodules and third-party dependencies require review.
records.license_notes: Keep repository licensing distinct from hosted services, implementation partners and submodules; no complete dependency-license inventory was performed.
records.maintenance_security: Active 3.2.x releases and current commits were observed. Security policy defines supported lines and private reporting; release notes reference SBOM/Trivy and testing work. These process signals are not a full audit.
records.interoperability: FHIR R4 laboratory resources/workflows, HL7 v2.5.1, ASTM/analyzer interfaces and OpenMRS/iSantePlus exchange are documented; this does not establish general clinic EHR conformance.
records.arabic_rtl: Localization infrastructure is active, but the reviewed official thread showed Arabic translation only beginning; completed Arabic coverage and RTL QA are unknown.
records.confidence: Medium-high for repository status, license, maintenance, deployment and interoperability; medium for clinic-workflow boundaries and Arabic/RTL readiness.

records.name: Medplum
records.clinic_fit: Infrastructure foundation for custom ambulatory/EHR products: FHIR data, auth, SDKs, React components, intake, charting, scheduling, referral and billing primitives. It is not a turnkey clinic system; several workflows require custom code or third-party providers.
records.license: Apache License 2.0 for repository source; OSI-approved. Hosted infrastructure, enterprise support, compliance assistance and custom work are separate commercial services.
records.license_notes: Preserve LICENSE and NOTICE; review third-party dependencies and integration-provider terms separately.
records.maintenance_security: Frequent 5.1.x releases and a published version policy indicate active maintenance. Security documentation describes practices and disclosure; no full self-hosted dependency or deployment audit was performed. The 36-month security-patch commitment applies to Enterprise customers, not automatically to OSS users.
records.interoperability: FHIR R4, US Core 5.0.1/USCDI v2, SMART 2.0, Bulk Data 2.0, OAuth2, HL7 V2, SFTP, CDS Hooks and FHIRcast are documented; verify exact profiles and enabled integrations.
records.arabic_rtl: No primary evidence of Arabic UI, translations or RTL layout was found.
records.confidence: Medium-high for license, architecture, APIs, deployment options and maintenance; medium for clinic-workflow completeness; low for Arabic/RTL and jurisdiction-specific clinical/regulatory readiness.
